data.review: CMA remains a solid and dependable invoicing platform, and due to its deep integration with financial processes it will likely be required until 2027/2028. However, its weaknesses are increasingly limiting. The system is slow, unstable, and prone to freezing—especially when accessed via virtual desktops—causing frequent disruption. Its interface is outdated, unintuitive, and lacks modern workflow features such as effective task management, mobility, or streamlined navigation. Even simple configuration changes require IT intervention, making the platform rigid and difficult to adapt. Ongoing data quality issues and fragile reporting also introduce operational risk, reinforcing the need for eventual replacement.
data.roadmap: CMA is now a legacy platform, being replaced where possible with the CLE / Adjuster Hub. Through 2026 it will still be an important system of record but it will increasingly function as a purely invoicing platform accessed only for detailed setup of the invociing process. The roadmap is to replace all Adjuster interactions with equivalent Adjuster Hub features and where possible build Admin functions into Adjuster/Admin Hub too. This will add Workflow capabilities for users (Cash Hub Invoicing Workflow and Client Notifications are 2 key examples).

data.name: Adjuster Hub
data.summary: Adjuster Hub is a core component of the Complex Loss Ecosystem and the strategic adjusting platform for CSI Adjusting. It underpins the future-state operating model, providing a single, extensible foundation for managing complex claims consistently across the business.
data.features: Recording Time, Managing Billing rules, Hosting performance dashboards

data.tech_stack:
Adjuster Hub is a cloud-native adjusting platform built on the Microsoft Azure stack, designed for scalability, resilience, and regional performance. The application layer is implemented using .NET 8, with Telerik UI for Blazor providing a rich, component-based user interface that supports complex workflows while maintaining a consistent and performant UX across devices.

The platform is deployed using a modular Azure App Services and Container Apps architecture, separating web, API, and background processing concerns to enable independent scaling and deployment. Azure Front Door and App Service Plans are used to manage ingress, traffic routing, and environment isolation across development, UAT, and production landscapes.

Operational data is stored in Azure Cosmos DB, which serves as the primary transactional data store. Cosmos DB is configured with multi-region geo-replication, allowing data to be hosted close to users in regions such as Australia East and Southeast Asia, delivering low-latency access, regional resilience, and automated failover.

Real-time application state, notifications, and collaborative updates are handled via Azure SignalR, enabling responsive, event-driven user interactions without reliance on polling. Supporting services include Azure Storage Accounts, Key Vault–backed certificate management, Application Insights, and App Configuration, providing observability, security, and configuration governance across the platform.
data.review:
Adjuster Hub is a cloud-native, modular claims handling platform designed to support complex loss and adjusting operations at global scale. Built on a modern Azure-centric architecture, it is composed of loosely coupled services that can be independently deployed, scaled, and evolved, allowing capabilities to be introduced or retired without impacting the wider estate.

The platform exposes functionality through well-defined APIs and event-driven patterns, enabling integration with core claims systems, finance platforms, document services, and external client or broker portals. This modular design supports rapid configuration by line of business, geography, or client, while maintaining a consistent underlying data and security model.

Adjuster Hub is engineered for global resilience and performance. It uses Azure Cosmos DB as its primary operational data store, leveraging multi-region geo-replication to provide low-latency access, regional failover, and high availability for adjusters operating across multiple territories. Data consistency and replication policies are tuned to balance responsiveness with transactional integrity for claims workflows.

Real-time collaboration and state synchronisation are delivered via Azure SignalR, enabling live updates to tasks, notes, and claim status across distributed teams without page refreshes or polling. Combined, these capabilities provide a scalable, resilient platform that supports modern adjusting workflows while reducing operational friction and long-term technical debt.
data.roadmap:
Adjuster Hub is a core component of the Complex Loss Ecosystem and the strategic adjusting platform for CSI Adjusting. It underpins the future-state operating model, providing a single, extensible foundation for managing complex claims consistently across the business.

The roadmap runs through to 2027 and is aligned to key operational and commercial outcomes. Planned enhancements focus on improving time recording, automated invoicing, and WIP capture to strengthen revenue assurance, reduce manual effort, and accelerate billing cycles through tighter integration with finance systems.

Further roadmap items include enhanced adjusting tools for structured case file management and improved data quality, ensuring consistent and reliable capture of critical claim information. In parallel, AI-enabled capabilities will be introduced to summarise case histories and generate client insights, reducing administrative overhead while improving transparency and client outcomes.

It uses multiple SharePoint sites (one per Adjusting Businesss Management Team) and an Outlook plugin from a vendor (MacroView) to auto route Case related emails into the correct Case sharepoint folder. Adoption has varied wildly with some teams using it and others not finding it useful enough to invest the time into setting it up. No tech issues with SharePoint but Macroview has had issues post Microsoft patching on Desktops/Outlook.
data.roadmap:
eCases will be eventually replaced by Adjuster Hub Document Management (AHDM) as part of the 2026 CLE roadmap. This will also replace MacroView Outlook plugin.
Since its inception the Adjuster Hub platform has been created and the Microsoft technology stack has improved. 
Coupled this with the AI revolution and there is signficant reason to plan to replace this platform with something more modern that will support the business into the next decade.

Adjuster Hub Case Management or eCases V2 will provide much improved user experience as well as offering a wider set of teams access to summarised data. Adjusting, Compliance, Commerical and Data teams will all benefit from a modern document (and workflow) platform. We expect to see findings from discoveries on the evolvement of Adjusting document management during Q2 with an expected start in Q3.
data.manual_alternative_process: Yes, copy files manually directly from Outlook to SharePoint folders
data.compliance_narrative:
The data parsed by the plugin and eventually stored within Sharepoint is broadly considered as 'Highly Confidential'. As such, the Sharepoint sites should be classified in accordance with the data it holds. Currently the underlying Sharepoint sites have not been classified accordingly. 

Sharepoint misconfigurations, unauthorized sharing, and improper use of sharing links are common sources of security breaches when using Sharepoint as a data store. A recent (May 2025) assessment of the CT Sharepoint environment against CIS benchmarks has found that improvements are required to apply more robust protections for data stored within Sharepoint.

The Business Continuity approach documented within the Manual Alternative Approach column should consider how the business will continue to operate in the event that Sharepoint is unavailable for a prolonged period. 

 
No known documented Business Impact Analysis and RTO/RPO documented for this application.

Full Infosec assessment of this business application is scheduled for Q3 2025.

The roadmap should be to replace the Cargo portal with Client Hub and the Access front end with a customised CLE configured module. FONDEN was first created as a budget line in the Federal expenditure budget of 1996, and became operational in 1999. Funds from FONDEN could be used for the rehabilitation and reconstruction of: 1) public infrastructure at the three levels of government (federal, state, and municipal); 2) low-income housing; and 3) certain components of the natural environment. FONDEN consists of two complementary budget accounts, the FONDEN program for reconstruction and FOPREDEN program for prevention, and their respective financial accounts. The FONDEN program for reconstruction is FONDEN's primary budget account. It channels resources from the federal expenditure budget to specific reconstruction programs. The FOPREDEN program for prevention supports disaster prevention by funding activities related to risk assessment, risk reduction, and capacity building on disaster prevention. The FONDEN system is continuously evolving to integrate lessons learned over the course of years of experience)

data.summary: Charles Taylor standard productivity tooling. Microsoft 365 is a product family of productivity software, collaboration and cloud-based services owned by Microsoft. data.review: Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel are cornerstone applications within Office 365, renowned for their versatility and powerful features. Word excels in document creation and editing, offering robust formatting tools and collaboration capabilities. PowerPoint is a go-to for creating dynamic presentations, with a wide array of templates, animations, and multimedia integration. Excel stands out for its advanced data analysis and visualization tools, making it indispensable for tasks ranging from simple calculations to complex data modeling. FinOps is the Group HR and Purchase Order platform. In 2025 PSA and CRM (CTI) are being removed, replaced with a custom cheaper project management process built directly in FinOps and CTI are migrating off CRM to Softland and CP4 hosted on the Inworx Domain. 

This is a solid platform based on the Microsoft Power platform. It is Microsoft's strategic platform for Finance and Operations. Things are made more difficult because we have 2 instances, one for CTI and one for Group HR. In 2025 we would like to rationalise to a single instance and ensure that the Purchase Order process works effectively alongside the HR instance. Migrating this from the CTI instance to the Group instance provides benefits in alignment of single source of truth, providing improved ability to account and recharge costs to the appropriate cost centres and business units. 

It is not clear whether Finance will decide to migrate all FinOps GL and PO processes into Sun 6
data.roadmap:
Further automation and improvements to the Purchase Order process are planned in Q2/Q3 to ensure that Purchases are better managed and tracked, giving the business forecast on costs. 

2025/01 - Discovery has been completed into further enhancing the process, such as building PowerApps for PR/Supplier Onboarding Requests and refining the process within ServiceNOW. Currently, only overhead costs have been moved to Dynamics FinOps PO, but the Finance team plans to migrate further processes. Options such as direct input into FinOps allows users to key information directly into the system, leveraging in-house FinOps SMEs for development, but requires Dynamics licenses for each user and may result in an inefficient user journey. Building PowerApps involves staging data in a database to be re-keyed into FinOps by P2P Analysts, offering dynamic information entry and removing dependency from ServiceNOW, but also requires Dynamics licenses and significant development resources. Eventually, B4B will be replaced.

Refining the process within ServiceNOW aims to improve the existing form with dynamic mapping of information, with P2P Analysts re-keying information into FinOps. This option involves minimal development costs but does not improve the speed of the process and maintains ServiceNOW licensing and dependency. Additionally, there is a requirement to integrate Dynamics with CMA and SUN to eliminate the manual processes currently in place.

data.name: Tide
data.summary:
Insurers around the world extend their distribution and ability to underwrite specialist risks, by delegating their authority to enter into contracts of insurance to expert third parties. These third parties, known as coverholders, provide businesses and individuals with a wide choice of different insurance covers.
 

Policies offered by coverholders can range from mainstream insurance such as motor or travel cover to specialist niches such as political risks or cyber-liability insurance. The use of these Delegated Underwriting Authorities (DUA) is extremely widespread. For example, a global network of over 4,000 local coverholders operates in and brings business to the Lloyd’s market. For insurers, it is essential that they have clear understanding of the risks their coverholders are underwriting, to ensure that they are holding sufficient capital to meet any associated claims. In practice, the flow of information to and from coverholders can be difficult to monitor and manage.

An insurer with multiple coverholders may receive many different reports, provided in a huge range of different formats, from simple spreadsheets to sophisticated electronic messaging. Charles Taylor InsureTech has developed a ground-breaking solution to the management of DUA. Our solution, called TIDE, has been developed in partnership with an insurance technology platform business majority-owned by the Group.

TIDE rethinks the way delegated authority information is handled to help brokers and insurers make data driven decisions and reduce processing and compliance costs. It takes information from any source, into a centralised cloud based platform which processes, standardises and validates data against rules at source, without the need for intervention. TIDE has been extremely well received and is already being trialled by insurers.

data.name: Dream
data.summary: Legacy financial accounting package. Used as a general ledger for both GoTrex case invoices and other expenditure.
data.support_narrative: Very limited issues recorded. Only current ongoing issue is that the Dream ledger PDF export process does not run properly on Citrix Windows 2019 clients. This is a significant issue for migration to AWS.
data.tech_stack: Vendor product runs on SQL 2000 which has been out of support for 15 years.
data.review:
Clearly a very old platform that needs to be migrated to Sun. Although it has been stable for a long period of time the risk of continuing to use Dream increases each year. Currently not part of the active GoTrex DR setup and any disaster event would require a rebuild which is becoming more of a challenge with very old and unsupported OS and SQL versions. The majority in Dream is also in GoTrex so in a worst case scenario we can work back from the GoTrex data, however running in this mode for any period of time would be very challenging. 
A discovery project was run in 2020 to look at migration path/costs and it was considered too expensive and complex at the time with other critical business activities and migrations taking priority. 
One particular complexity would be the fund/float ledger which we do not have a direct replacement for with Sun (would need to be designed). Potentially this could be a simpler setup using a reconcilliation report and comparison to client bank statements, to reduce this futher some clients could be migrated onto the Vitesse platform (self manage float) which doesn't touch the Dream float.
Another area of complexity is the historical transaction data going back 13 years. We would question the need to migrate this data and therefore a simple archive may suffice, this would dramatically reduce the overall migration effort. 
The current GoTrex/Dream integration would need to be migrated to the Sun API. Many other systems are integrated using this (XML based) API. 
As this is currently a one-way integration this would be much simpler than something like CMA (which is 2 way). The mapping exercise between Dream nominal codes and ledger accounts into Sun is probably the main challenge but not a huge piece of work. Setting of clients in GoTrex will need to be syncd with Sun 6 suppliers, initially this can be a manual process. A decision would need to be made on non-claim related invoices/ledger, this is also relevant to the current AWS Migration / Citrix Windows 2019 PDF issue.


Post AWS move Chris Gundry comments:
•	SQL3/Dream runs on Server 2003, which is an end of life, unsupported OS, with various security issues. Aviva etc all raise issue with this in audits as everyone knows.
•	The SQL version is SQL 2000 which is also end of life and not well supported by the various teams due to its age. Options around its backup and interaction with it are also limited as a result, which might make querying data from it more problematic.
•	The Dream application itself/the scheduled task associated with the involving fails randomly, requiring the server to be restarted. This issue has been going on for years and no one has got to the bottom of it, because there is no support from CODA/Dream and the NIS element of the interaction is bespoke.
•	The Finance team cannot currently access invoice (?) files on SQL3 due to SMBv1 limitations in AWS WorkSpaces where they work. Manual action is being done by the Dev team to mitigate this until Dream is migrated to a new platform. This ties up Dev resource etc. and cannot be automated due to the same SMBv1 restrictions. It could be bypassed by reducing security overall, but that is obviously not desirable.

Additionally, we have some issues that came out of the AWS migration, which I have outlined previously at various points, and were deemed as issues for ‘AWS Phase 2’ as Softcat did not address them as part of the migration and deemed them out of scope.
•	Server 2003 is not supported by AWS DRS, so has no warm standby server, which did previously exist OnPrem via Veeam. If AWS AZ1 becomes unavailable, then the only option is to restore the server from an AWS backup.
•	AWS Backup does not support Server 2003, so there is no application consistent backup and backups are therefore ‘crash consistent’ and restores have potential for data loss. The backup is daily only, so any data entered between failure and last backup would be lost regardless.
•	Server 2003 only supports SMBv1, so SQL cannot be configured to take native backup to the AWS FSx storage like the other SQL servers now have to in AWS (previously this was done via Veeam OnPrem). Again, there are ways around this, but none of them are desirable in terms of security, complexity, manageability or cost.
•	Due to no application consistent backups being taken, the SQL logs are not being truncated currently, which long term can lead to running out of disk space. I suggested changing the SQL DB mode and a few other options, but as yet no decision was made.
•	When the SQL3 server initially moved to AWS, it failed to boot reliably, despite migrating it via several different methods. This logically shouldn’t have happened, and didn’t happen in the UAT testing. But Softcat and AWS were unable to explain why it was happening during the final migration, and without access to the underlying AWS platform there was little we could do. Luckily, we tried one other method to get another copy of the server to boot, and it worked. Essentially this was the same as the previous methods, so made very little sense that it worked. There is no guarantee that this booting issue will not happen again in the future, as it was not confirmed why it happened in the first place. If it does, then we could expect a prolonged outage of the server and little help from AWS as the system is unsupported.

data.name: InRehersal
data.summary: InRehearsal is a digital training platform designed to support experiential learning through structured rehearsal and feedback. It enables users to practice real-world scenarios in a safe environment, supporting role-play, guided exercises, and facilitated sessions. The platform helps organisations develop skills such as communication, leadership, and decision-making by combining interactive content with reflection and coaching. InRehearsal supports both individual and group learning formats and can be used for live, blended, or remote training programmes. Its focus is on improving confidence, consistency, and performance through repeated practice and targeted feedback.
data.tech_stack: InRehearsal is delivered as a cloud-based SaaS platform, accessible via modern web browsers without the need for local installation. It is designed for secure, scalable use across organisations, supporting remote and distributed users. The platform includes user management, session scheduling, content delivery, and data capture within a centrally managed environment. As a SaaS solution, InRehearsal benefits from regular updates, managed hosting, and built-in security controls, reducing operational overhead for customers while ensuring availability, performance, and compliance with standard data protection requirements.
